title: Secure Link Shortener & Analytics Service Requirements Specification
problem_statement: The business requires a greenfield URL shortener service that enforces security controls (SSRF protection, protocol restrictions, domain denylisting, link expiration, and abuse rate limiting) while providing privacy-preserving marketing insights (aggregate click counts, 30-day UTC daily trend, and top referrer domains without storing IP addresses or full user agents).

requirements.text: The service must only accept target URLs using HTTP or HTTPS schemes during link creation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a link creation request with target URL 'https://example.com/page', the service accepts the URL and returns a shortened link with HTTP 201.

Given a link creation request with target URL 'ftp://example.com' or 'javascript:alert(1)', the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request and an error message indicating unsupported scheme.

requirements.text: The service must prevent Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) by validating that target URLs do not resolve to loopback, private RFC 1918/RFC 4193, link-local, or cloud metadata IP addresses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a link creation request with target URL 'http://127.0.0.1/admin', 'http://localhost:8080', or 'http://[::1]', the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Given a link creation request targeting 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' or a DNS name resolving to a private/link-local address (e.g., 10.0.0.1, 192.168.1.5), the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request.

requirements.text: The service must reject target URLs whose domains match an administratively configurable malware and phishing denylist.
acceptance_criteria: Given that 'malicious-domain.com' is present in the active denylist configuration, when a user submits 'https://malicious-domain.com/login', the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request.
Given that 'safe-domain.com' is not on the denylist, when a user submits 'https://safe-domain.com', the service accepts the request and generates a shortened URL.

requirements.text: The service must support link expiration, defaulting to 90 days from creation, while allowing an explicit per-link expiration date/duration at creation time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a link creation request without an explicit expiration parameter, the link record is saved with an expiration timestamp set to 90 days (7,776,000 seconds) after creation.
Given a link creation request with an explicit expiration of 14 days, the link record is saved with an expiration timestamp set to 14 days from creation.
Given a request to access a shortened URL whose expiration timestamp is in the past, the service returns HTTP 410 Gone (or HTTP 404 Not Found) and does not perform a redirect.

requirements.text: The service must enforce rate limiting on link creation per client to prevent spam and resource exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client sending link creation requests within the allowed quota (e.g., up to 60 requests per minute), all requests return HTTP 201 Created.
Given a client exceeding the configured creation rate limit within the time window, subsequent creation requests receive HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a 'Retry-After' header.

requirements.text: The service must redirect visitors of an active, valid shortened URL to its target destination using a non-permanent redirect to allow visit tracking.
acceptance_criteria: Given an active shortened link pointing to 'https://example.com/dest', when an HTTP GET request is received for the link, the service returns HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect with the 'Location' header set to 'https://example.com/dest'.

requirements.text: The service must record analytics on each redirection and expose an insights endpoint providing total clicks, clicks per UTC day for the last 30 days, and top referrer domains.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request to GET '/api/links/{id}/insights' for a link with 5 recorded clicks over 2 distinct UTC days, the response returns HTTP 200 with total clicks = 5 and a breakdown by UTC date for each day within the 30-day window.
Given clicks originating with Referer header 'https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=123', the analytics endpoint aggregates the count under the referrer domain 'news.ycombinator.com'.

requirements.text: The service must not store personal data (specifically no IP addresses and no full user-agent strings) in analytics or persistent storage.
acceptance_criteria: When a shortened link is visited, the database record created or updated for analytics contains only aggregated counts, UTC date, and sanitized referrer domain; inspecting the database proves no client IP addresses or raw User-Agent headers are persisted.

requirements.text: The service must expose health check and operational telemetry endpoints for service monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Given a GET request to '/healthz', the service returns HTTP 200 OK and database connectivity status.
Given traffic with SSRF or denylist blocks, internal metrics counters for security rejections are incremented.

assumptions: HTTP 307 or 302 redirects will be used instead of HTTP 301 to ensure client browsers do not cache the redirect and bypass click tracking.
Rate limiting will evaluate client IP addresses in volatile memory (e.g., Redis sliding window) without storing raw client IP addresses in persistent databases.
Referrer domains are extracted from the HTTP 'Referer' header by parsing the hostname and discarding path, query, and userinfo components to prevent sensitive data leakage.
Direct visits with no 'Referer' header will be recorded under a 'direct' or 'none' category in referrer analytics.
Links that reach expiration will not be purged immediately from the database to retain analytics history, but will cease redirecting.

open_questions.question: What is the maximum allowed custom expiration period for a shortened link?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines input validation rules on link creation and affects long-term storage retention capacity.
open_questions.proposed_default: A maximum expiration limit of 365 days from creation.

open_questions.question: How many top referrer domains should be returned by the marketing insights endpoint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Defines the API response contract and query limit for the referrer aggregation endpoint.
open_questions.proposed_default: Top 10 referrer domains ordered by click count descending.

open_questions.question: What client identifier should be used for link creation rate limiting in the absence of user accounts, and can client IPs be processed ephemerally in memory?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Clarifies the security architecture to guarantee compliance with the zero-PII constraint while preventing abuse.
open_questions.proposed_default: Use ephemeral, one-way hashed client IP addresses in an in-memory cache with a 1-minute expiration window.

out_of_scope: User accounts, registration, login, and multi-tenant access control.
Geographic location tracking and IP-to-geo resolution.
Custom branded domains and custom vanity slug editing.
